newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway minister quits over spy scandal.
newsitem.headline: Norway minister quits over spy scandal.

text.p: Norwegian oil and energy minister Grete Faremo resigned on Monday in a scandal over the national intelligence service's surveillance of a prominent left-wing politician.

Faremo was justice minister when the intelligence service in June last year started looking into the background of Berge Furre, a member of a parliamentary committee assigned to examine the work of the intelligence service itself.
"Minister Faremo has today told me that she takes the constitutional responsibility for the ministry's handling of the surveillance of Berge Furre," Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland told parliament.
"She has today submitted her resignation. I have accepted it."
Hans Olav Oestgaard, head of the intelligence service, also announced he was stepping down.

It was the second time in less than three weeks that a minister was forced to resign from Jagland's Labour minority government, which took power on September 25 following the resignation of veteran Labour premier Gro Harlem Brundtland.

National Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen, who quit as a U.N.-appointed Middle East mediator to join the new Norwegian government, resigned on November 27 amid a storm of media criticism over alleged irregularities in a share option deal he profited from 10 years ago.

Analysts said Jagland was forced to show strength and unceremoniously dump Faremo, a tough politician and a government minister since 1992, in view of the media hunt for scapegoats and increasingly vocal opposition calls for her to resign.
Norway was shaken last year by revelations about the government's systematic registration of communists during the Cold War.
The left-leaning Labour Party was severely criticised by the opposition and media for cooperating with the security police in keeping watch on communists in the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

Furre, who broke with the Labour Party in the 1950s to help found the Socialist Leftist Party (SV), which is represented in parliament, last summer joined the parliamentary watchdog assigned to look into the Cold War monitoring of communists.

Last week a declassified intelligence report revealed that the intelligence service had sought information in June last year from the former East German Stasi security policy files on Furre. He continued to be under investigation in the autumn.
Faremo, who says she was not aware that a member of the spy watchdog was himself being investigated, said last week "I fell off my chair" when she read the report.
SV parliamentary leader Kjellbjoerg Lunde said Faremo's resignation came as no surprise to her.
"It is my hope that we will now get a thorough investigation so that we shall have an intelligence service that does the job it is supposed to be doing in a democracy," she said.
